title: Cross-Company Convening — Agenda & Prep Notes (v0.1)
content:
Purpose:
This doc scopes a half-day cross-company convening intended to align exec updates, surface draft company OKRs for Q2–Q3, and surface operational asks for product launches (Hosted API features + Dedicated ramp). This is a working agenda — we expect slides and pre-reads to land from each org lead by EOD Mar 2.

High-level goals for the convening:
- Get executive alignment on the 3 prioritized company OKRs and the top 6 supporting KRs (decision-oriented, not exploratory).
- Validate launch readiness checklist for Dedicated capacity expansion (customer-facing SLAs and pricing).
- Surface cross-team blockers (infra, observability, docs, legal) that would prevent a clean rollout or an all-hands announcement.
- Produce a finalized run-of-show and comms plan for the company all-hands (internal + customer comms) within 5 business days.

Attendees (invited):
- CEO, COO, CTO (required)
- Heads: Eng (Serving Runtime, Platform), Product (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private), Developer Experience, Applied ML, SRE, Security & Compliance, GTM leads (Growth, Sales AE lead), Customer Success lead, People Ops (for comms cadence)
- Optional: Solutions Eng reps from active pilot accounts

Pre-reads (deliverables & owners):
- Draft company OKRs (one-pager) — Aisha P. (attached link above)
- Dedicated launch readiness checklist — Marco C. (due Mar 2)
- Latency and infra capacity snapshot (P95/P99 trends, capacity projections) — Evelyn B.
- Comms draft for all-hands — Ruth Z.
- Top-10 customer escalations / unresolved risk list — Samir O.

Draft agenda (half-day, 3.5 hours + buffer) — target: Mar 9, 09:00–12:30 PT
- 09:00–09:15 — Framing: why this convening matters and decision outcomes (CEO)
- 09:15–09:45 — Exec health-checks (5m per exec area, tight Q&A) — deliverable: one-line ask/ask owner at end
- 09:45–10:30 — OKR presentation + focused debate (present draft OKRs, propose 3 prioritized)
    - Decision checkpoint: choose O1 and O2 (yes/no/on-hold)
- 10:30–10:45 — Break
- 10:45–11:15 — Dedicated ramp readiness & risks (infra + SRE deep-dive)
    - Decision checkpoint: green / yellow / red to proceed with next booking tranche
- 11:15–11:50 — Cross-team breakout roundtables (2 simultaneous rooms):
    - Room A: Observability & Rollouts (Console + Tracing + Rollbacks)
    - Room B: Customer comms & Sales enablement (pilot handoff, enablement docs)
    - Each room: produce 3 action items with owners and ETA
- 11:50–12:10 — Synthesis and open issues log (facilitator)
- 12:10–12:30 — Next steps, owners, and comms timeline (People Ops + CEO)

Decision matrix (what we expect to arrive at):
- Finalize top-2 company OKRs and the three supporting KRs for each (measurable targets + owner).
- Decide on go/no-go for next Dedicated capacity tranche (binary + conditional mitigation items).
- Approve the all-hands run-of-show and the public-facing talking points for the CEO and VP Sales.

Draft company OKRs (v0.1) — these are intentionally narrow and decision-focused:
- Objective 1: Make Redwood the predictable, economical inference partner for ML teams
  - KR1.1: Reduce average per-token hosted inference cost by 18% through batching + quant savings (owner: Eng-Optimize, Marco C.)
  - KR1.2: Increase Hosted API active product integrations from 120 -> 180 (owner: Growth, Priya N.)
  - KR1.3: Ship two model-variant fallback policies in runtime (owner: Serving Runtime, Evelyn B.)

- Objective 2: Own reliability for production inference at scale
  - KR2.1: Meet P95 latency SLOs for core hosted endpoints < 120ms for 8/10 traffic windows (owner: SRE, Samir O.)
  - KR2.2: Reduce production incidents causing customer-visible degradation by 40% (owner: Platform Eng)
  - KR2.3: Complete GA of console route-level tracing and cost breakdown (owner: Product Console, Ruth Z.)

- Objective 3: Enable enterprise adoption of Dedicated & Private options
  - KR3.1: Close 6 new Dedicated contracts (committed capacity) with minimum ARR $X — target pilot conversion (owner: Sales AE Lead)
  - KR3.2: Create a hardened Private deployment checklist and KMS integration playbook (owner: Security & Compliance)
  - KR3.3: Ship automation for Dedicated autoscaling policies (owner: Platform Eng)

Open questions we want the convening to settle:
- Is the 18% cost reduction target realistic without materially impacting response quality? (needs evaluation from Applied ML)
- Do we need a separate compliance gating checklist for EMEA Private deployments before go-to-market? (Legal + Security input)
- Which customers are prioritized for the next Dedicated tranche (top-down selection vs. sales-pipeline-driven)?

Key risks and contingencies (preliminary):
- Infra capacity: If autoscaling automation slips, we need a throttled onboarding runway (ops-playbook).
- Customer expectations: Announcing Dedicated broadly without solid SLAs could create churn risk — recommend a staged announcement tied to contract terms.
- Comms: Messaging must be explicit about intended performance improvements vs. aspirational roadmap items.

Pre-meeting asks for each owner (one-liners due Mar 2):
- Execs: Prepare a 60s health statement + one hard ask that requires cross-org input.
- Eng leads: One-slide capacity plan and any dependencies that need exec clearance.
- Product: Proposed comms snippet (30–40 words) for external audience.
- SRE: Incident trends and a proposed mitigation for the top recurring incident class.

Post-convening follow-ups (timeline and ownership):
- Day 0–2: Finalized OKR doc (Aisha) and decision log published to Confluence.
- Day 3–5: All-hands slide deck + script finalized (Ruth + CEO) and rehearsed.
- Day 5–10: Cross-team action tracker with owners and weekly 15-min async status updates (facilitator: Marco).

Success criteria for the convening (how we will know it worked):
- Executive sign-off on O1 and O2 with named owners and measurable KRs.
- A concrete go/no-go decision on Dedicated tranche with mitigations listed and owners assigned.
- A signed-off run-of-show for the all-hands and a comms plan assigned to People Ops.

Notes to self / facilitation tips:
- Keep discussions timeboxed; use a visible timer.
- Capture dissent as action items with owners, not as parking-lot notes.
- We want crisp decisions, not consensus on low-impact items.

Appendix: rough run-of-show speaker list (first draft)
- CEO: framing + top-level announcement
- CTO: tech readiness and risks
- VP Product (Hosted API): feature status + customer impact
- Head of Sales: customer pipeline and go-to-market notes
- Head of SRE: P95/P99 and incident reductions
- People Ops: comms and rehearsal logistics

Attachments to prepare (by Mar 2):
- OKR one-pager (Aisha)
- Dedicated readiness checklist (Marco)
- P95/P99 trend deck (Evelyn)
- All-hands comms draft (Ruth)
- Pilot customer risk list (Samir)

Open/parking lot items (will be triaged post-convening):
- Long-term model-cost playbook (defer to Optimize team deep-dive later Q2).
- Detailed SLA legal review for multi-region Private (requires legal team allocation).

If you are an owner listed above: please upload your one-pager to the linked Confluence page and drop a note in the #company-convening slack thread with a short status update. If you cannot make the convening, nominate a delegate and note the name in the calendar invite.

-- end --
